card.name: End of a phrase before a stop-use statement
card.fires_on: The last word of a noun phrase that is about to be followed by a rule or consequence, such as 'discoloration', 'excipients' or 'formulation'. It is seen mostly in contraindication and discontinuation sentences.

modes.label: Contraindication list end
modes.description: Final word or piece of an allergy-to-ingredient phrase, just before the period.
modes.example: Patients who have had a known serious or severe hypersensitivity reaction to ENTYVIO or any of its exc<<ipients>>. ( 4 )

modes.label: Visual inspection warning
modes.description: The word 'discoloration' ending a particulate-matter condition, followed by 'should not be used'.
modes.example: Product with particulate matter or discolor<<ation>> should not be used. BRIVIA

modes.label: Condition before a dosing action
modes.description: The end of a clinical condition just before an instruction to interrupt, stop or switch.
modes.example: Grade 3/4 nausea and/or vomiting despite optimal anti-emetic<< therapy>> Interrupt RYDAPT for 3

card.writes: It slightly favors words of intent such as 'intended' and 'wanted' and disfavors words of choice such as 'chosen' and 'opted'.
card.plain: It marks the end of a condition or ingredient phrase in a label, just before the sentence says what to do or not do.
